flip: Importing pre-made staves of heading 4416 instead of raw lumber into Mexico
reasoning: New charred white oak barrels are classified in 4416.00.3010. Under 19 CFR 102.20, heading 4416 requires a shift from any other heading. Foreign oak lumber (4407) and steel hoops (7212/7326) shift to 4416 when crafted into barrels in Mexico.

key_factors: (b) single failing material imparting essential character
decisive_step: Manufacture of the receiver dryer subassembly in China
flip: Manufacture the receiver dryer subassembly in Canada or the United States
reasoning: Both the imported Chinese receiver dryer subassembly and the finished unit are classified in subheading 8421.39, failing the 102.20 tariff shift rule in Canada. Under 102.11(b)(1), the single failing material (the receiver dryer) imparts the essential character, conferring Chinese origin.

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to heading 1302
decisive_step: Blending guar gum and xanthan gum in Mexico
flip: Xanthan gum predominating by weight so product classifies in 3913.90 without shifting
reasoning: As a GRI 3(b) mixture of 80% Mexican guar gum (1302.32) and 20% Chinese xanthan gum (3913.90), the product is classified in 1302.32. Under 102.20, a shift to heading 1302 from any other chapter is required. The Chinese xanthan gum shifts from Chapter 39 to Chapter 13 in Mexico.

key_factors: (a)(1) wholly obtained or produced as waste and scrap in Mexico
decisive_step: Generation of gold waste, scrap, and dust from jewelry manufacturing in Mexico
flip: Generating the waste and scrap from manufacturing operations performed in the United States
reasoning: The gold waste, scrap, and polishing dust are classified under subheading 7112.91.01, HTSUS. Under 19 CFR 102.1(g)(9), waste and scrap derived from manufacturing operations in a country are wholly obtained or produced there, conferring Mexican origin under 102.11(a)(1) (or 102.11(a)(3)).

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to heading 8528
decisive_step: Assembly of HUB PCBA, LED blocks, and components into display cabinets in Mexico
flip: Classify a non-originating material under heading 8528 or 8540
reasoning: The LED display cabinets are classified under heading 8528 (specifically 8528.59). The 102.20 rule for 8528.59 requires a change from any other heading, except 8540. Because all non-originating materials are classified outside 8528 and 8540, all foreign materials shift under 102.11(a)(3) in Mexico.

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to 8414.59
decisive_step: Final assembly of the fan blower in Mexico
flip: Import an incomplete fan assembly already classified in subheading 8414.59 into Mexico
reasoning: Under 19 CFR 102.20, subheading 8414.59 requires a change from any other subheading. Unlike USMCA GN 11(o) which requires a heading change, the foreign housings and impeller (subheading 8414.90) and electric motor (heading 8501) satisfy the subheading shift in Mexico.

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to heading 7113
decisive_step: Casting gold links and assembling bracelets in Mexico
flip: Cast the gold bracelet links in the United States instead of Mexico
reasoning: The 14K gold bracelets are classified in heading 7113 (7113.19). In Mexico, US alloyed gold (7108), US steel springs (7320), and foreign diamonds (7102) are cast and assembled into bracelets, satisfying the 102.20 tariff shift to heading 7113 from any other heading.

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to subheading 9018.90
decisive_step: Manufacturing the thermocouple subassembly and assembling the RF probe in Mexico
flip: Import pre-made RF probe under 9018.90 into Mexico for mere packaging
reasoning: The RF probe is an electro-surgical/medical instrument classified under 9018.90.6000. All foreign materials (steel hypo-tubes of Ch. 73, wires/cables of 8544, connectors of 8536, plastics of Ch. 39) are outside heading 9018 and satisfy the 102.20 tariff shift in Mexico.

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to heading 6406
decisive_step: Manufacturing and forming of the hockey skate inserts in Canada
flip: Using foreign footwear parts of heading 6406 that fail the tariff shift
reasoning: Removable hockey skate inserts/insoles are classified under subheading 6406.90. Assuming production occurs in Canada from non-heading 6406 materials, all foreign inputs satisfy the 19 CFR 102.20 tariff shift rule under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3), conferring Canadian origin.

key_factors: (b) single failing material imparting essential character
decisive_step: manufacture of the base belt in Taiwan
flip: Manufacture the base belt in Canada from non-heading 4010 rubber and textile materials
reasoning: The finished endless conveyor belt with vulcanized profiles remains in heading 4010 (4010.12). The 102.20 rule for heading 4010 requires a shift from any other heading. The Taiwanese base belt (4010.12) fails to shift in Canada, imparting essential character under 102.11(b).

key_factors: (b) origin of failing parts imparting essential character
decisive_step: Molding of plastic doll components in China
flip: Molding the plastic doll components in Mexico instead of China
reasoning: The doll and its parts are classified in heading 9503. The 102.20 rule for 9503 requires a shift from another chapter, or from parts if not by simple assembly. Screwing and gluing in Mexico is simple assembly, so Chinese parts fail. Under 102.11(b)(1), origin is China.
